summary.whatChanges: In the tRPC jsonl stream consumer, reads for promise and async-iterable chunks now check the reader's `done` flag. If the stream ends cleanly before the expected chunk arrives, a clear `Error('Stream closed unexpectedly')` is thrown/rejected instead of a confusing `TypeError` from destructuring `undefined`. Regression tests cover both cases.
behaviorChanges: Truncated streams (clean EOF mid-iteration) now reject pending promises with 'Stream closed unexpectedly' instead of 'value is not iterable' TypeError
Async iterables from a prematurely closed stream throw a descriptive Error when iteration continues past the last received chunk
Consumers no longer risk hanging/looping on `undefined` chunk values after stream end
risks: Error is a generic `Error` with a hardcoded message, not a typed/tRPC error, so callers can only match on the string
Code that previously relied on the TypeError (or on silent behavior) when a stream truncated will now see a different error type/message
